question:
A class investigates how two parameters affect the system $x+y+z=3$, $x+ky+2z=4$, and $x+2y+kz=m$. The coefficient determinant depends on $k$, while the right-hand side of the third equation depends on $m$. The students want to classify the system according to whether it has one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solution, paying special attention to values of $k$ for which the coefficient determinant becomes zero.

(a) Evaluate the coefficient determinant in terms of $k$.

(b) Determine the values of $k$ for which the system has a unique solution.

(c) Examine the system when $k=0$ and classify it according to $m$.

(d) Examine the system when $k=2$ and classify it according to $m$.
explanation:
(a)
The coefficient determinant is
$$D= egin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\1 & k & 2\1 & 2 & k\end{vmatrix}$$
Expanding along the first row,
$$D=(k^2-4)-(k-2)+(2-k)$$
$$D=k^2-2k=k(k-2)$$

(b)
The system has a unique solution when $D eq0$. Therefore,
$$k(k-2) eq0$$
Hence, the system has a unique solution for
$$k eq0\quad ext{and}\quad k eq2$$

(c)
When $k=0$, the system becomes
$$x+y+z=3$$
$$x+2z=4$$
$$x+2y=m$$
From the first two equations,
$$z-y=1$$
Let $y=t$. Then $z=t+1$, and from $x+2z=4$,
$$x=4-2(t+1)=2-2t$$
Therefore,
$$x+2y=(2-2t)+2t=2$$
Thus, the system is consistent only when $m=2$. For $m=2$, it has infinitely many solutions
$$x=2-2t,\quad y=t,\quad z=t+1$$
For $m eq2$, the system is inconsistent and has no solution.

(d)
When $k=2$, the last two equations become
$$x+2y+2z=4$$
$$x+2y+2z=m$$
They are compatible only when $m=4$. For $m=4$, subtracting the first equation from the second gives
$$y+z=1$$
and hence $x=2$. Let $z=t$. Then,
$$x=2,\quad y=1-t,\quad z=t$$
Thus, the system has infinitely many solutions when $m=4$. For $m eq4$, it is inconsistent and has no solution.

options.A:
(a) $D=(k-1)(k-2)$
(b) Unique solution for $k\neq1,2$
(c) At $k=0$, infinitely many solutions when $m=4$
(d) At $k=2$, infinitely many solutions when $m=2$
options.B:
(a) $D=k(k+2)$
(b) Unique solution for $k\neq0,-2$
(c) At $k=0$, infinitely many solutions for every $m$
(d) At $k=2$, the system always has a unique solution
options.C:
(a) $D=k(k-2)$
(b) Unique solution for $k\neq0,2$
(c) At $k=0$, infinitely many solutions when $m=4$ and none otherwise
(d) At $k=2$, infinitely many solutions when $m=2$ and none otherwise
options.D:
(a) $D=k(k-2)$
(b) Unique solution for $k eq0,2$
(c) At $k=0$, infinitely many solutions when $m=2$ and no solution when $m eq2$
(d) At $k=2$, infinitely many solutions when $m=4$ and no solution when $m eq4$
